To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the majority of pharmacy students have a basic experience of IT resources on entry to the university, and that the provision of suitable IT training for students is likely to enhance the use of these resources during the first semester of the course.

the use of IT by first year pharmacy students was found to be enhanced by: • the availability of IT resources; • the availability of suitable training; • the use and availability of CAL; and • the availability of the Internet.

• students entering pharmacy school have a basic level of experience of IT; • students are willing and eager to embrace the use and application of IT in the classroom; • IT is used more by students for learning in some subjects than others; • students are more willing and eager to use IT for learning in some aspects of their learning than in others; • students who have a greater experience of IT before entering the university are more willing and able to use IT for their learning.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the implementation of IT resources for student learning and the development of the student’s IT skills and attitudes.
the use of IT in pharmacy education and the impact of the use of IT on student performance.
the implementation of information technology for learning in a first year undergraduate pharmacy course.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IT is not a panacea for teaching and learning, but can be a useful adjunct to teaching methods and can be a useful learning resource for students.
the use of IT in pharmacy education is a positive step towards the enhancement of the student experience of pharmacy education and the development of a more effective learning environment.
IT is a useful tool in the learning process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IT can enhance the student learning experience and the development of the course, but only if students have the skills, knowledge and confidence to use the IT resources available to them.

• students are willing to use IT resources to assist their learning; • the implementation of IT resources in this course has had a significant impact on student learning and the teaching of the curriculum; • the use and implementation of IT resources has been enhanced by the provision and development of suitable IT resources.
the implementation of IT into the curriculum has been a success, but there is a need for further training of students to enable them to use IT resources to their full potential.
The main takeaway from our work is that
students will benefit from the provision of IT training in a variety of ways and the provision of such training is likely to be a worthwhile investment.
students are not necessarily computer literate on entry to university.
the students are keen to learn how to use IT and are keen to use it for learning and that this can be facilitated by providing them with appropriate training and resources.
